# Phantom — the engineering agent workbench

> Full documentation bundle for agents. Everything below is plain Markdown.

## Overview

Phantom by AshlrAI: the open-source engineering agent workbench for CLI accounts, local models and autonomous fleets.

Package: `@ashlr/phantom` v3.30.0.
Node.js floor: >=22.15.0.

## Install

```sh
npm install -g @ashlr/phantom
ashlr --version
ashlr verse
```

ashlr verse prints a read token and a mutation token; the server listens on
`127.0.0.1` only. Neither token is written to disk.

## Commands

- `ashlr --help`: top-level command list
- `ashlr verse`: serve the console
- `ashlr docs --agent`: agent cheat sheet (plain text)
- `ashlr docs --agent --json`: command registry as JSON

## Use-case guides

### [Coding agents on local models · Phantom use cases](https://verse.ashlr.ai/use-cases/local-models)

Run coding agents on local models with Phantom: Ollama discovery, llama-server dispatch through a normalizing proxy, measured token and wall-clock numbers from the repo.

### [Bring your own agent accounts · Phantom use cases](https://verse.ashlr.ai/use-cases/own-accounts)

Drive the coding-agent CLIs and accounts you already use: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Devin and local models. One workbench, pinned profiles, real usage readings.

### [Review every agent change · Phantom use cases](https://verse.ashlr.ai/use-cases/review-agent-work)

Review AI agent changes before they land: per-turn checkpoints, per-file and per-hunk accept and reject, undo and rewind previews, and a recorded decision log in Phantom.

### [Autonomy inside a scope you sign · Phantom use cases](https://verse.ashlr.ai/use-cases/signed-autonomy)

Phantom autonomy ships dormant and runs only inside a standing grant you sign with Touch ID: an eight-stage ladder, the same merge gates every time, reversible merges and a hash-chained ledger.

## Comparison

- [Phantom vs. driving each agent CLI directly · Phantom](https://verse.ashlr.ai/compare/agent-clis): An honest comparison of driving each coding-agent CLI directly versus running them inside Phantom, with every vendor statement linked to a public source and every Phantom claim linked to the repository.
